title: Measure the voltage between two named terminals with a multimeter and its test probes
instruction: Measure the DC voltage between the L terminal and the N terminal with the multimeter: the meter must show it steadily for at least one second while one probe's tip is held in each terminal's test opening. Do not put a probe tip into any other terminal's opening.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, about 0.8 million US workers) and industrial machinery mechanics (49-9041.00, about 0.4 million) routinely test circuits with voltmeters: switch the meter to the right range, then hold its two probe tips on two terminals at once until it reads. On a crowded terminal strip each tip must reach the right clamp and stay there; probing the wrong terminal measures the wrong circuit.
setup: A steel TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail, 500 mm long, fixed flat on the table (open side up, left to right), its centre 0.30 m in front of the arm bases on their midline. Latched on it at its middle, 40 polyamide screw-clamp terminal blocks side by side, 5.2 mm apart centre to centre, each 56 mm long across the rail and 40 mm tall; from the left: green-yellow, grey (L), 35 beige, blue (N), green-yellow, beige. L is 96.2 mm left of the rail's centre, N 91.0 mm right. On top of every block at its middle, a test opening: a 2.6 mm square hole, 8 mm deep, with a 45 degree funnel at its mouth (1.5 mm, 1.0 mm at the sides), its floor the metal clamp. A regulated 12 V DC adapter (SELV, 12 V +-5%) is wired into the L (+) and N (-) clamps only. A handheld autoranging 6000-count digital multimeter in a dark grey rubber holster (170 x 90 x 44 mm, 450 g) lies face up, taped down, 0.17 m in front of the arm bases on the midline, display (22 mm digits) toward the strip; its rotary selector (40 mm knob, 38 x 8 x 9 mm grip bar) starts at OFF and clicks clockwise through V~, V DC, mV, Ohm, 30 degrees apart, about 0.12 N m per click. Two black plastic holders (30 mm cubes, an 8 mm hole in the top) fixed 0.20 m in front of the arm bases, 0.14 m left and right of the midline; in them, tip down, a red probe (left) and a black probe (right), each 140 mm long, 30 g: 2 mm steel tip 15 mm long, 6 mm shroud, 16 mm finger guard resting on the holder, 10 mm handle 100 mm long, a 1 m silicone lead plugged into the meter (red in V, black in COM).
scoring: Read from the meter's display (a reading twice a second; on V DC it shows 12.00, or -12.00 with the probes swapped, only while the two tips touch the L and N clamps at once, else 0.00). At the end of the run: 0 if a probe tip ever entered any other terminal's test opening (1 mm or more below its mouth). Otherwise: 1.0 if, with the selector on V DC, the display showed the test voltage (11.40 to 12.60 V, either sign) at three readings in a row (at least 1 s), both probes held in the grippers at each; 0.5 if it showed the test voltage at one reading at least, both probes held; 0.25 if a held probe's tip was put into the L or N opening 4 mm or more below its mouth; 0 otherwise. A tip touches a clamp when inside the bore within 0.3 mm of the opening's floor (8 mm down). Real trial: the display in the video; the strip's video for the tips.
reset_notes: Turn the selector back to OFF; stand the probes back in their holders, tip down. Nothing is consumed. The 12 V source stays wired to L and N; the meter stays taped down.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. No electricity is simulated: a tip touches a clamp when within 0.3 mm of its opening's floor, and the display shows 12.00 V while both tips touch the L and N clamps. The rendered display takes 2-3 s to settle; the scored reading changes at once. The 1 m leads are not simulated. Fixed meter case; the selector is a jointed knob with spring clicks. Generic terminal blocks (fixed, 2.6 mm square test openings); probes collide as square sections.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,600 steps; arms moved about, never grasped a probe or turned the selector; display blank); scripted demo: 1.0 (selector to V DC, both tips on the L and N clamps, meter showed 12.00 at three readings in a row, success at step 550).
